statement: Let m = len(edges). The function returns a result r. Exactly one of the following holds. (A) r is empty, and for every function w mapping each index i with 0 <= i < m and edges[i][2] = -1 to an integer in [1, 2*10^9], the shortest distance from source to destination in the undirected graph with nodes 0..n-1 and edge list E_w (whose i-th edge is [edges[i][0], edges[i][1], edges[i][2]] if edges[i][2] > 0, and [edges[i][0], edges[i][1], w(i)] otherwise) is not equal to target. Here distance is the minimum sum of edge weights over all paths from source to destination. (B) r is non-empty, for every j with 0 <= j < len(r) we have len(r[j]) = 3, and there is a bijection pi from {0,...,len(r)-1} to {0,...,m-1} such that for every j: the unordered pair {r[j][0], r[j][1]} equals {edges[pi(j)][0], edges[pi(j)][1]}; if edges[pi(j)][2] > 0 then r[j][2] = edges[pi(j)][2], and if edges[pi(j)][2] = -1 then 1 <= r[j][2] <= 2*10^9; and the shortest distance from source to destination in the undirected graph with nodes 0..n-1 and edges r is exactly target.
preconditions: n, edges, source, destination, target satisfy: 1 <= n <= 100; 1 <= len(edges) <= n*(n-1)/2; each edges[i] has length 3; for every i, 0 <= edges[i][0] < n, 0 <= edges[i][1] < n, edges[i][0] != edges[i][1], and (edges[i][2] = -1 or 1 <= edges[i][2] <= 10^7); 0 <= source < n, 0 <= destination < n, source != destination; 1 <= target <= 10^9; the undirected graph with nodes 0..n-1 and an edge {edges[i][0], edges[i][1]} for each i is connected; no two edges have the same unordered endpoint pair (no repeated edges).
